# The Tale of the First Shadow

In the beginning, when the world was newly formed, there existed only brilliant light. The Sun Goddess, Solara, illuminated every corner of existence, leaving nothing hidden. All creatures lived in constant brightness, and they grew weary, for they could never rest their eyes.

"Great Goddess," Corvus said, "your light is magnificent, but all beings grow exhausted. Might there be respite?"

Solara pondered this. She realized that constant light, though beautiful, was indeed harsh. She plucked a single feather from Corvus and cast it to the ground. Where it landed, darkness bloomed—the very first shadow.

"This is my gift," Solara declared. "Wherever my light meets solid form, shadows shall provide rest for weary eyes."

Corvus was transformed, his feathers turning black as the shadow itself. To this day, ravens carry darkness in their plumage, reminding all creatures of the balance between light and shadow, and the wisdom of knowing when to seek each.

Enraged by her rejection, the Sun blazed with terrible fury. "Then you shall never create in my light again!" The Sun's heat burned so intensely that Lyra's form darkened, flattening against the ground.

Yet even transformed, Lyra continued her art. As a shadow, she followed every living thing, weaving herself to their forms, creating silhouettes of endless variety. She danced on walls, stretched across valleys, and played with children who chased her changing shapes.

Thus shadows were born—not from darkness, but from a weaver who chose love of earth over the glory of heaven, teaching us that true art finds expression even in the most unexpected forms.
